# CHAPTER 5: RESONANCE OF THE LOST

**The tides have shifted. Following a daring and successful mission to the ancient derelict VEILED SHADOW, Team Gamma has returned to the Altisian fleet with life-saving technology and a prize beyond measure: the SEVENTH MOON, a freighter brought back from the dead.**

**But the victory is tempered by a haunting discovery. The Wayfinder recovered on Bespin is no mere map—it is a KEY. And the VEILED SHADOW is its LOCK. Aboard the ship, an ancient Force-ghost has named the young Mandalorian, WES DEL-FIN, as the PATHFINDER, tasked with reawakening a hidden network of Force-conduits that could lead the Jedi to a sanctuary far from the reaches of the rising EMPIRE.**

**Amidst the heavy weight of destiny, a flicker of light remains. MARINA CLOUDSPINNER, Wes’s partner and the mother of his unborn child, has been raised to the rank of JEDI KNIGHT. Now, with the fleet’s survival hanging on a razor’s edge, the team plunges back into the treacherous KARTHON EXPANSE. Their mission: to turn the key, harmonize the ship’s heart, and reclaim a legacy that has waited in the silence for four thousand years....**

The blue-white tunnel of hyperspace outside the *Seventh Moon’s* viewport is a steady, mesmerizing blur. Inside the cockpit, the atmosphere is a study in quiet, professional preparation. The ancient Ghtroc freighter feels significantly more robust than it did during its maiden flight out of the derelict; the reinforced mandible plating and the tuned capacitors provided by Chief Gaxx’s teams have smoothed out the ship's previously erratic vibrations.

Wes sits in the co-pilot's chair, the weight of the Wayfinder case resting just behind him, a silent anchor in the Force. Marina sits behind him in at the operations station, her movements confident and precise as she monitors the core's stability. Behind them, in the main hold, the "Fixer" droids sit in their magnetic cradles, their single eyes dark and unblinking.

Kaelen leans back in the pilot’s, his hands resting lightly on the control yokes, his grey eyes fixed on the time-to-reversion clock. **"She’s handling like a different ship, Wes,"** he grunts, his voice carrying a rare note of genuine satisfaction. **"The forward drift is gone, and the power coupling isn't screaming at me every time I adjust the pitch. Gaxx’s team knows their business."**

He glances at the nav-comp. **"We’re coming up on the end of the primary leg to clear Karthos Prime’s shadow and then the jump through 'Korta’s Passage'. Travel time will be just under four hours. We're right on schedule."**

Leaning back into the copilot's chair Wes let out a slow breath.   Outside the viewport he watched the blue-white hyperspace tunnel.   He wondered what, if anything, would be different when the Wayfinder was used to travel between the known spacelanes.  It was something that they would have to wait to find out.  There was still the job of freeing the *Shadow* from the *Whispers* to tackle first.  


He listened to and felt the two others next to him.   Next to him in the pilot's chair was Kael.   The pilot was calm and measured as always.   The team had come to trust the man’s skill and ability behind the controls of whatever he flew.   


Sitting right behind Wes was Marina.   He could feel the confidence within her.   It felt like the promotion the Council gave her solidified her confidence.  She, like all of them, had been through some rough times.  Doubted herself yet took the chance to leave it all behind to come to the Praxium.   He turned toward the center, the chair rotated with him and he looked at her.   He smiled when she turned and gave him a quick look and smile.  She was quick to back so she could  monitor the readings. 


Kael’s movements had Wes turning back to the front.   The pilot was comfortable.  Wes would even say somewhat at ease considering where they were heading back to.   As Kael spoke about the ship Wes understood the  man's feelings.  Wes nodded as he tapped on his control panel.  **”They put a lot of work into her for us.”**  He shifted gears and followed up on the flight path mentioned.   **”Will we be able to use the same corridor as before?”**

Kael shifts slightly in his seat, his hands making minute adjustments to the sublight trim even while in hyperspace. He taps a series of calculations on his secondary screen before answering. **"The 'Korta's Passage' leg is fixed coordinates, so that stays the same. But the sublight approach through the Graveyard Shallows is a different story. Commander Heston’s data confirmed that the *Shadow* has a slow, unpredictable drift. The debris field out there isn't static either."** 

He glances at Wes, his expression grimly professional. **"I've updated the entry vector based on Korta’s latest projections. We’ll be aiming for the same quadrant, but I’ll have to fly the final kilometers on visual and short-range sensors again. If the drift has shifted the hangar's orientation, we might have a trickier time getting into that maintenance alcove than we did before."**

Wes looked at the plotted course and the projected, possible drift of the  *Shadow.*  Kael was right, it could be tricky.  **”Understood.  Less than four hours.”**  He tapped on his bracer to set a timer for three hours.   **”When we reach the Graveyard Shallows we can reassess the approach vector.   We’ll need eyes on it before we can make any final approach decisions.  Keep us updated.  I’ll check back and let me know if you need a break.”**  Wes gave the seasoned pilot a nod, grabbed his helmet and stood.  **”Also since we’re not boarding a hostile ship this time would you like to join the team?   Your skills could prove useful in any number of places.”**


He looked at Marina who was still looking over the operations station.  **”Shall we go talk plans with the others for the reintegration of the Wayfinder to the *Shadow?*”**

Kael grunts, his eyes never leaving the blue-white tunnel of hyperspace. **"I appreciate the invite, Wes, but I’m a pilot. My place is here… in the chair. If things go sideways, you'll want the engines already hot."**

Marina unplugs her datapad from the operations station and stands, her movements slightly stiff after the period of intense focus. She smooths her robes over the subtle curve of her abdomen.  **"He's right, Wes. Having Kael on the bridge is a security measure in itself."** She offers a warm, tired smile, her presence in the Force steadying. **"Let's go. Sera and the others are likely finished with their initial gear checks by now."**

Wes and Marina descend the short ladder from the cockpit, moving through the ship's compact neck into the main lounge and engineering hub. The *Seventh Moon* feels different today—the oppressive layer of ancient dust is gone, replaced by the faint, sharp scent of cleaning solvents and fresh hydraulic fluid. The lighting here is bright and steady, reflecting off the clean metallic surfaces. 

In the central lounge area, the rest of Team Gamma has claimed the available space. Roric is seated on a cargo crate, methodically running a diagnostic on his ion rifle, the weapon's power cell humming softly. Echo is standing near the primary ramp, her gaze fixed on a small holographic display projecting the *Veiled Shadow’s* interior map. Sera is perched on the edge of the circular lounge seating, her legs swinging as she taps away at her specialized slicing rig, which is currently tethered to one of the ship’s auxiliary data ports.

Wes gave Kael an affirmative nod.  He understood the pilots and Marina’s reasoning.   **”Undersrood and vigilant eyes on the ship and our path of egress, if needed, is a good thing.”**  He gave Kael’s shoulder an affirmative thump.  The same he’d done numerous times with fellow Mandalorians.  Though this time not nearly as hard since the pilot wasn’t wearing armor.   


At Marina’s mention of the others he smile.  **”Lead the wash Cyar’ika.  I want to know what Sera and the others have planned for the return trip.”**  Sera was an expert slicer and now that she had an idea of what to expect on the *Shadow.*  He expected she would be even more prepared this go around.   

Less than a minute later the two of them were entering the central lounge.   There, the  rest of the crew was located in different positions.  All seeing totasks that were important to the mission.  


Sera looked up from her slicing rig as her legs continued to swing back and forth.   The Zeltron, always seeming to be in a good mood, smiled.   Wes smiled back as he walked near Marina.   **”Were four hours from dropping out of hyperspace we here we’ll begin our flight path to the *Shadow.*”**


He looked at the team he was taking back into the massive ship that was somehow part of his past.  Some long forgotten tradition that was one reawakened.  He steadied himself within the Force.  It was something that he knew Marina would sense through their bond.   **”I’m happy you're all here and coming back with us.”**  He said looking at Marina quickly before looking back.  **”I'm guessing this second time around we are a little more prepared.  Updates?”**  He asked looking at Roric and then to Exho and Sera as they each finished.
